newsitem.title: USA: BHP Copper US labor talks fail to reach deal - USWA.
newsitem.headline: BHP Copper US labor talks fail to reach deal - USWA.

text.p: Weekend talks between management of BHP Copper's U.S. operations and the United Steelworkers of America failed to reach any agreement and arbitration is set to be the next step, a union official said.
Both sides met in Houston July 12 and 13.
"There was not any progress made to speak of," USWA lead negotiator Robert Guadiana said. "So the parties are looking at interest arbitration right now."
"There was a lot of good discussion but we just didn't get there," Guadiana added.
No further meetings with BHP were scheduled but further talks could be held before arbitration, Guadiana said.
A BHP spokesperson was not immediately available.
Guadiana said more details about the labor talks would be released in a USWA press statement later.
Employees at BHP's San Manuel and Pinto Valley operations in Arizona, formerly part of Magma Copper, have a 15-year framework contract which is updated every five years.

If agreement is not reached in the current round of updating, the whole process must go to interest arbitration with the outcome binding on both sides for a year, during which there is no right to strike, union officials have said.
